home.headline: Dealer-level work on your Porsche or BMW.

home.final_heading: Call the shop. You'll talk to a technician.

approach.heading: How a job goes here
paragraphs: You talk to the technician who'll work on your car, not a service writer. We drive it with you if we can, then put it on the lift and call before we touch anything.
Every estimate is written and itemized, with the parts we'd use and why. If something can wait, we say so and note it, so you can plan for it instead of being surprised by it.
When you pick up, you get photos of what we found, the old parts if you want them, and a stamped service book.

about.heading: Factory-trained. Independent since 1991.
paragraphs: Erik Linde spent nine years as a master technician at a Porsche dealer in Stuttgart and Denver before opening his own four-bay shop on Valmont Road in 1991.
His son Jonas and three technicians work alongside him now. Between them they've seen just about every way a German car can go wrong, and how to fix it so it stays fixed.

testimonials.quote: Erik found an oil leak the dealer had missed twice, fixed it for less than their diagnostic fee, and showed me the old seal.
testimonials.author: Mark T.

testimonials.quote: I bought my 911 on the strength of their pre-purchase inspection. Thorough, honest, and they talked me out of the first car I looked at.
testimonials.author: Priya S.

testimonials.quote: Thirty years of owning German cars and this is the best shop I've used.
testimonials.author: Dan W.
